title: Strong quantum IOPs with polynomial communication
formal: Does every QMA promise problem admit a constant-round strong quantum interactive oracle proof with a uniform polynomial-time verifier, total prover-message length polynomial in the input length n, total query complexity \(O(1)\), completeness at least \(2/3\), and soundness at most \(1/3\)? The strong access model is defined below. The prover may be computationally unbounded, and soundness quantifies over all prover strategies.
why: The problem isolates the communication price of an extremely limited quantum verifier. A positive result would eliminate the exponential communication in the present strong construction.

progress.text: The general qIOP has polynomial communication but uses a polynomial private quantum resource. The strong construction operates on constantly many qubits but communicates $\exp(\operatorname{poly}(n))$ qubits. Question 1.9 asks for polynomial communication.

status_note: Literature checked on 10 September 2026; dates and review scope are recorded below.
review_note: The statement and listed results were individually checked against the cited sources. New proofs were not independently verified. The assessment of importance is editorial.

context_blocks.text: A quantum proof can be much larger than the portion a verifier actually inspects. An interactive oracle proof lets a prover supply such messages over several rounds, with the verifier charged for the qubits it touches. Communication volume and access complexity are therefore different resources.

The strong model requires the verifier to hand each received quantum message back in full and forbids sending an additional quantum message of its own. It still has private workspace. Returning a message does not mean undoing the measurement or channel applied to the queried qubits; the resulting state can be returned.

For example, a protocol might inspect only two qubits from an enormous register. That has constant query complexity but still transmits the enormous register. Conversely, allowing the verifier to retain part of a received message changes the protocol model even if the amount of communication is small.

The existing constructions meet different combinations of the desired bounds: general qIOPs have polynomial communication, while the strong construction has exponential communication. The question asks for polynomial communication in the strong model itself. The constant-round requirement and constant total query budget must hold together.

definitions: In each round the prover supplies a quantum register W. The verifier chooses queried positions through a measurement and applies a quantum channel only to those qubits and its private register; query cost counts accessed message qubits, summed over rounds. It returns the entire W register, may send additional classical information, and sends no additional quantum register. It can retain its own private workspace, but cannot retain any part of a prover-message register. The parties have no initial shared entanglement. Total prover-message length counts the full incoming registers, not only queried qubits. This restates the strong model of Definitions 5.1–5.2 and 5.13–5.15.
answer_criterion: Construct such a protocol for every QMA promise problem, or prove that at least one QMA promise problem has no protocol meeting all these bounds. Polynomial communication in the weaker general qIOP model does not suffice.

importance.reason: Tests how far succinct interactive verification can extend to quantum proofs with explicit communication restrictions; affects a broad proof-system design space.

category_assignment.reason: Mapped from the existing subject category

sentences: Interactive oracle proofs let a verifier inspect only selected parts of much larger prover messages.
This question asks for constant-round quantum versions that verify all QMA promise problems with polynomial total communication and only constantly many queries.
The strong quantum access model is part of the target, because different ways of querying quantum messages permit different verification strategies.
Soundness must cover arbitrary prover behavior, while the verifier remains efficient and has a constant completeness-soundness gap.
The project probes how far proof compression and local checking can extend when the evidence itself is quantum.
